newsitem.title: UK: Bankers get Eurotunnel debt report.
newsitem.headline: Bankers get Eurotunnel debt report.

text.p: Channel tunnel operator Eurotunnel's biggest creditors met in London Friday to get details of a financial restructuring plan agreed in principle earlier this week.

The meeting, lasting around four hours, took place at the offices of NatWest Markets, investment banking arm of National Westminster Bank, a member of the six-strong steering committee which negotiated the deal.
Banking sources said the committee made a presentation of the deal to the next tier of 26 "instructing banks" who represent the rest of Eurotunnel's 225 bank creditors.
"Obviously, no agreement was reached and everyone will now go back and look at the deal," said one banking source

The steering committee reached agreement with Eurotunnel earlier this week on a restructuring plan designed to ensure the company's long-term future and reach a solution to its gargantuan 9 billion British pounds ($14 billion) debt.

Details of the deal are expected to be released Monday when Eurotunnel holds news conferences in both Paris and London. This is expected to lead to the return of Eurotunnel shares to the markets from which they were suspended last Monday.

Analysts say around half of the firm's total debt must be retired in some way for the company to have a viable future and even then some feel it will still be a struggle depending largely on Eurotunnel's ability to raise prices while keeping market share on the cross-Channel route.
